extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, agents, IP offices, and intellectual property lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, examining, registering, publishing, opposing, transferring, renewing, cancelling, and enforcing trademarks before the Organization and competent domestic courts under the Annex. Includes requirements for joint ownership, collective marks, licensing, invalidity, restoration, and urgent remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint owners' right to use the mark with fair compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the joint owners may use the mark to his benefit, provided he makes fair compensation to the other joint owners who are not personally using the mark or who have not granted licenses for the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties cannot agree on compensation, the competent domestic court shall fix it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint owner may institute counterfeit proceedings with notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the joint owners may institute proceedings for counterfeit to his exclusive benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint owner who institutes such proceedings shall notify the other joint owners of the action. Any ruling shall be held in abeyance until proof of such notification is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting non-exclusive licenses by joint owners with compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the joint owners may grant to a third party a non-exclusive license to his benefit, provided he makes fair compensation to the other joint owners who do not personally use the mark or who have not granted licenses for the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amicable agreement on compensation fails, the competent domestic court shall fix the compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft license notification and offer to assign share
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft license agreement shall be notified to the other joint owners, together with an offer to assign the share at a specific price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within three months of notification, any joint owner may oppose the granting of the license provided he acquires the share of the person who wishes to grant the license; failing agreement, price fixed by court; parties have one month from notification of judgment to relinquish grant or purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive license requires unanimous consent or court leave
rubrics_metrics.description: An exclusive license may only be granted with the agreement of all the joint owners or by the leave of the competent domestic court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of share and right of first refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Each joint owner may, at any time, assign his share. Joint owners shall enjoy a right of first refusal within three months of the notification of the intent to assign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties fail to agree on price, the competent domestic court shall fix it. Parties have three months from notification of judicial decision (or in event of appeal) to waive sale or purchase; costs borne by waiving party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment of share by joint owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint owner may notify other joint owners that he is relinquishing his share to their benefit. With effect from entry in the special registry or notification to the Organization, the relinquishing owner is relieved of obligations and the remaining owners distribute the share in proportion to their rights, unless otherwise agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for registration shall be filed with the Organization or with the Ministry responsible for industrial property in accordance with Article 8, this Annex and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application file required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file shall contain: (a) an application addressed to the Director-General; (b) document proving payment to the Organization of requisite fees; (c) reproduction of the mark, including a clear and exhaustive list of goods or services with corresponding Nice Classification classes; (d) regulations fixing conditions of use for collective marks; (e) priority document, if applicable; (f) unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of registration by class
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark may be registered for one or more classes of goods and/or services as set forth in the Nice Agreement (International Classification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing report and transmittal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A report shall note each filing and specify the date and time of submission; a copy is issued to the applicant; the Ministry shall transmit documents to the Organization within five working days of the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim filing deadlines and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: To avail of priority of an earlier application, file with the Organization within six months of the previous filing date. Within three months of filing, attach a written declaration stating date/number/country/name of earlier application and a certified true copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple priority claims require compliance for each, payment of a fee for each right, and proof of payment within the three-month period. Priority documents received more than three months after filing entail loss of priority right, though reinstatement may be possible; refusal to restore is appealable within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date admissibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall grant as the filing date the date of receipt provided the application contains: (a) information allowing identity of applicant to be established; (b) express or explicit information on whose basis registration is sought; (c) reproduction of the mark and goods or services; (d) information concerning payment of filing fee; (e) statement as to whether an agent has been appointed and agent's name/address if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application for which requisite fees are not paid within one month of filing shall be considered withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication content for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each application: (a) filing number; (b) filing date; (c) reproduction of the mark; (d) goods/services with classification; (e) company name and applicant's name and address; (f) any priority claimed; (g) name and address of agent, if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition period and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months of publication, any person may oppose registration by submitting a written statement setting out reasons based on infringement of Articles 2 and 3 of the Annex, or of a prior registered right, or based on a prior application or earlier priority filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization sends copy to applicant who may reply within three months (renewable once). Organization may hear parties before ruling. Ruling appealable within 60 days. Organization shall only refuse application if opposition is well-founded. Final decision on forfeiture published in Official Bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a mark has been filed by a person who knew or should have known another had a prior right, that other person may file a claim of ownership within three months following publication of the first filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization sends copy to applicant who may respond within three months (renewable once). Hearing available. Ruling appealable within 60 days. Organization shall not transmit application to claimant unless claim is well-founded. Final ruling recorded in special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division (divisional applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial application concerning several goods/services may be divided into divisional applications at least until decision on registration, during opposition/claim proceedings, or during appellate processes concerning those decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division may only concern list of products/services. Divisional applications retain filing date and priority benefit. A fee is payable for each divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination criteria and rejection grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For every application the Organization shall examine whether formal conditions (Article 9) have been met and requisite fees paid. Any filing not meeting requirements of Article 3(a), (c), (d) and (e) shall be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with formal deficiencies (except certain fee paragraph) are irregular and applicants invited to regularize within three months (extension 30 days for proven necessity). Failure to regularize leads to rejection. Rejection issued by the Director-General. No rejection under specified paragraphs without opportunity to regularize. Organization may rectify obvious clerical errors. Legal date of registration is filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may appeal to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days of notification of the rejection decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of registration contents
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of registration, the owner shall be furnished a certificate containing: registration number; application number; filing date; reproduction of the mark; statement of classes under Nice Classification; goods/services to which mark applies; company name or owner name/address; validly claimed priority, if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish the information stipulated for each certificate of registration together with name and address of agent, if applicable, and enter it into the special registry of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations fix procedures for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is valid for 10 years from filing date; ownership may be preserved indefinitely through successive renewals effected every ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal may be secured by application filed during the last year of the 10-year period on payment of prescribed fees. A six-month grace period after that year is allowed subject to payment of a surcharge. Renewal does not entail fresh examination. Entry and publication of renewal noted. A mark not renewed may not be registered for identical/similar goods/services by a third party within three years following expiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to special register information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may, after publication of application or registration, on written application and payment of requisite fee, obtain information, excerpts or copies from the special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: International protection via Madrid Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is filed with or registered by the Organization, an applicant/national or resident or having real/effective establishment in a Member State may ensure protection of the mark on territory of Contracting Parties of the Madrid Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for implementation fixed by implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: After registration, the owner may renounce registration wholly or for some goods/services at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renunciation must be notified by registered letter with acknowledgement to the Organization, which enters and publishes it. If a license is recorded, renunciation entered only on submission of licensee consent unless licensee expressly waived that right in contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture for non-use and genericide
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic court may order deregistration where the mark, for an uninterrupted period of five years prior to the request, has not been used on territory of a Member State if owner fails to provide valid grounds; or where by owner's action it has become the usual designation (genericide). Cancellation may apply to all or some goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner bears burden of proof regarding use. Use by another person recognized as use if endorsed by owner. Final removal communicated to Organization and published. Registration deemed never to have had effect after removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity of registration by courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic courts may declare invalid registration on request of Public Prosecutor or interested person/group if registration does not conform to Articles 2 and 3 or conflicts with a prior right (invalidation for prior right only at request of owner of prior right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity may apply to all or some goods/services. Final decision notified to Organization for entry and publication. Registration deemed invalid as from date of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where protection is not renewed owing to circumstances beyond control of owner, owner or entitled persons may apply for restoration on payment of renewal fee and surcharge within six months of cessation of circumstances and no later than two years from due renewal date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include statement of grounds and proof of payment. Organization examines and may restore or reject. Restoration does not extend maximum duration. Restored marks published. Rejection appealable within 60 days. These paragraphs also apply where application was not filed within treaty time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability and formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights in a mark are transferable in whole or in part. Acts involving transfer, licensing, assignment, pledge or cancellation of pledge must be evidenced in writing on pain of invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers/licensing may relate to all or some of the goods/services. Validity of licensing of exploitation right may be territorially limited to a Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability against third parties requires registration of acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers, licenses and other acts shall not be enforceable against third parties unless recorded in the special register of marks and published in the Official Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization shall furnish copies of register entries, records concerning pledges, certificates attesting absence of entries, and identity certificates reproducing mark information on request and subject to conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: License contract formalities and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may grant a license enabling a natural or legal person to use the mark for all or some goods/services. Duration of license may not exceed registration duration. License contract must be in writing and signed on pain of invalidity and entered in the special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License is not enforceable against third parties until entered and published. License removed from register on proof of expiry/termination. Unless otherwise stipulated, grant of a license does not preclude licensor from granting other licenses (subject to notifying licensee) or from using the mark. Grant of an exclusive license precludes licensor from granting other licenses and, absent contrary provisions, from using the mark himself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid clauses in license contracts (anti-competitive restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses in license contracts that constitute anti-competitive practices or impose restrictions not deriving from registration rights or not necessary for upholding such rights shall be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not considered restrictions: (a) restrictions relating to extent, scope or duration of exploitation of the mark or the quality of goods/services; (b) obligation on licensee to abstain from acts liable to impair validity of registration. Unless otherwise provided, license not assignable and licensee not authorized to grant sublicenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court recognition of invalid license clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic court may establish invalid clauses at request of any person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations governing use for collective/collective certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall fix the conditions for use of collective marks and collective certification marks. Protection shall not encompass such marks whose regulations are contrary to public policy or morality. Organization shall reject amendments contrary to public policy or morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of nature of mark (collective vs certification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mark must be designated on application and in the certificate as a collective mark or a collective certification mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and registration of changes to regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner of a collective mark or collective certification mark may communicate changes to regulations governing the mark; an indication of such change shall be entered into the special register on payment of requisite fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may own a collective mark
rubrics_metrics.description: The State, public companies, unions/groups of unions, associations or groups of producers/manufacturers/craftsmen/tradesmen may own collective marks provided they are officially recognized and have legal personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and supervision of collective marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective marks shall be affixed either directly by the owning group as means of control, or by members on goods/objects traded by them; such use shall be under supervision of the group and in accordance with governing instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense rights for members of collective mark owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member of the group owning the collective mark may institute civil and criminal proceedings provided he proves failure of the group to act and calls on it to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and conditions for collective marks transfer and invalidity grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective marks shall neither be assignable nor transferable, except on legal merger authorized by Ministry. A court may declare a collective mark invalid or forfeit where owner has ceased to exist, rules governing use are contrary to public policy or morality, mark does not fulfill required conditions, or owner knowingly used/allowed use contrary to rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If declared invalid/forfeit, mark may not be appropriated or used; after 10 years from final decision it may be registered by a group with same nationality as previous group. Final decision communicated to Organization and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective certification mark filing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A collective certification mark may not be filed by any person who is neither the manufacturer, nor the importer, nor the seller of the goods or services to which the collective mark pertains. (text contains bracketed [not] indicating possible OCR uncertainty)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploitation conditions for collective certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploitation of collective certification marks shall be open to any persons (aside from the owner) who provide goods or services meeting conditions stipulated by exploitation regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer restrictions for collective certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: A collective certification mark may not be assigned, used as a pledge, or for other enforcement, but Ministry may authorize transfer of registration provided beneficiary assumes responsibility for actual control of exploitation; transfer entered in special register and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity and forfeiture of collective certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic court may declare invalid or forfeit a collective certification mark where owner has ceased to exist, regulations fixing conditions are contrary to public order and morality, mark does not meet requirements, or owner knowingly allowed use contrary to regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where invalidity or forfeiture is declared, mark may not be deposited or used for same goods/services. After 10 days from final decision it may be registered in this regard. Final decision communicated and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent courts and procedure for actions concerning marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil actions concerning marks shall be brought before competent domestic courts and heard as for summary matters. In criminal counterfeiting cases competent criminal court shall rule on challenges relating to invalidity, expiry, or ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before domestic courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a mark is registered by a person who knew or should have known another had priority, the other may claim ownership before competent domestic court. Where mark acquired in infringement of legal/contractual provision, prejudiced party may claim ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision transferring the mark communicated to Organization and entered in registry; licensees notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts prior to publication not prejudicial (subject to recording/prosecution after notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts prior to publication of the application may not be considered prejudicial to rights attaching; however, acts subsequent to notification to alleged counterfeiter of official copy of application may be recorded and prosecuted; court shall hold ruling in abeyance until registration is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfeiting as infringement and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of rights of owner as defined constitutes counterfeiting. Counterfeiters incur civil and criminal liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterfeiting may be proven by any means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgent measures to prevent infringement (preliminary relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with locus standi may make an urgent application to competent court seeking orders to prevent imminent infringement or continuation of alleged counterfeiting, including orders against intermediaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order urgent measures ex parte where delay would cause irreparable harm; for ex parte measures, evidence reasonably accessible to applicant must make it likely rights are being infringed or infringement imminent. Court may order seizure, prohibition, or transfer of suspected infringing products, and require guarantees to secure compensation if measures are later found unjustified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-measure procedural requirement (10 working days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where measures to stop infringement are ordered prior to proceedings on the merits, the applicant must file proceedings (civil or criminal) within 10 working days after the day the measure is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise, on defendant's application the measures shall be cancelled (defendant not required to justify), without prejudice to damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure procedure and required proof/security
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner or exclusive right holder may request a bailiff/public/judicial officer (assisted by expert if applicable) to make detailed inventory, with or without seizure, following an order by presiding judge within whose jurisdiction operations are to be conducted (including at border).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order made on application and submission of proof of registration. Where grounds for seizure exist, order may require applicant to make a security deposit adequate without deterring applicants; security deposit always required of foreigners. Person in possession must be given copy of order and proof of deposit on pain of invalidity and damages against officers and customs official.
